summary: Explored hyperparameter/schedule tuning within the fixed baseline architecture (depth 8, no width/depth changes). Raising Muon MATRIX_LR alone (0.04->0.06) gave a small, noisy improvement (0.996697). The dominant lever turned out to be shrinking TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2^19 to 2^18 tokens/step (more, noisier optimizer steps in the fixed 5-minute budget), which alone took val_bpb from baseline 0.997359 to ~0.989-0.993; combined with a modest Muon LR bump to 0.045 (not 0.06, which was worse at this batch size) it reached my best of 0.990382. Shortening WARMDOWN_RATIO (0.5->0.3) hurt, and pushing batch size down further to 2^17 is untested (crashed on a divisibility assertion against DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE*MAX_SEQ_LEN, would need DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE lowered too). Next steps: retune DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE downward together with TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to properly test whether the noisier-optimizer-steps trend continues, and re-sweep MATRIX_LR/WARMDOWN_RATIO jointly at the 2^18 batch size since LR and warmdown appear coupled to batch size rather than independently tunable.
